articles.summary: Run open-weight models like DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi K2 on your own hardware, then reach them securely from anywhere through Pangolin's AI gateway - no API keys, no data leaving your infrastructure.
articles.title: Self-Host DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi K2: Private Access From Anywhere

articles.summary: Give engineers and coding agents access to a self-hosted vLLM or Ollama cluster from one endpoint, authenticated by identity instead of API keys passed around a team.
articles.title: vLLM and Ollama Clusters: Secure Remote Access Without a VPN

articles.summary: Access your NVIDIA DGX Spark from any laptop without SSH, a VPN, or an open port. Run Ollama on the Spark and reach it through Pangolin's identity-aware AI gateway, from the same endpoint you use for cloud models.
articles.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark Remote Access: Run Inference From Anywhere

articles.summary: A general-purpose guide to putting any self-hosted model server - vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, LocalAI, or a private downstream gateway - behind Pangolin's identity-aware AI gateway.
articles.title: How to Connect Any Self-Hosted AI Model to Pangolin

articles.summary: Pangolin 1.22 introduces an AI Gateway for cloud and self-hosted models with identity-aware access. SSH, RDP, and VNC public resources, plus SSH and HTTPS private resources, are now available in Community Edition.
articles.title: Pangolin 1.22: AI Gateway for Cloud and Self-Hosted Models
